title: Finite etale filtration and trace transfer for lower-shriek sheaves
statement: Let k be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], X a reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], j:U -> X an open immersion, r a prime, R = ULift(Z/rZ), and G a finite locally constant R-module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] on U. Let v:V -> U be finite etale. Suppose v^*G [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] has a specified finite filtration W_0=0, W_n isomorphic to v^*G, with monic inclusions and each cokernel the constant R sheaf R on V. Suppose the unit G -> v_*v^*G [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] has a specified retraction. Assume all eight assertions [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions] for extension by zero of constant R from every open in every reduced separated finite-type k-curve of dimension at most one. Then all eight assertions hold for j_!G [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. No connectedness or degree hypothesis on v is needed after supplying the filtration and retraction.

proof.text: Apply Zariski main theorem to j composed with v and replace the finite compactification by the reduced closure of V. Etale over reduced implies V reduced, so V remains a dense open in the reduced compactification Y. Finiteness gives the separated finite-type curve structure and the dimension bound by integral incomparability. The inclusion V -> p^{-1}(U) is finite by permanence over a separated scheme; hence its dense open image is closed and is all of p^{-1}(U). A surjective open immersion is an isomorphism, giving the cartesian square.

The constant-case hypothesis gives assertions for j'_! R on Y. Exact extension by zero and short-exact devissage inductively establish them for the finite filtration, beginning with the zero object, and the terminal isomorphism gives them for j'_! v^*G. Finite pushforward and its exchange with extension by zero identify the resulting sheaf with j_! v_*v^*G.

Apply j_! to the unit and its specified retraction. For nonzero r-torsion sheaves the primary characteristic condition forces p=r; invertible-order torsion forces r invertible in k, otherwise G is zero and its pullback and pushforward are zero. Constructibility is preserved by finite locally constant pullback, finite pushforward and extension by zero. Thus the larger sheaf has the required conditional hypotheses. Cohomology retractions preserve vanishing and finiteness, and the natural comparison maps are retracts preserving bijectivity and surjectivity. Descend all assertions to j_!G.

proof_origin: Stacks 03SD, paragraphs 2--4: compactify the supplied finite etale cover, devissage its supplied filtration and descend through its supplied unit retraction. The constant case is a hypothesis, not reproved or assumed as the conclusion.
